items.readable_text:
Content:
In this lesson, we will learn how to divide larger numbers by two-digit numbers with remainders using the relationship between multiplication and division.

Content:
To begin with, let's figure out how to compute [MATH: 47\div 13.]

Content:
We will start by computing products of [MATH: 13] and other whole numbers, starting from [MATH: 1,] until we get to a number that is greater than [MATH: 47\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: 13 × 1|= 13; 13 × 2|= 13 + 13 = 26; 13 × 3|= 26 + 13 = 39✓; 13 × 4|= 39 + 13 = 52×([math]> {47}[/math], so too big)]

Content:
So, [MATH: 13 \times {\color{blue}3}] is smaller than [MATH: 47,] but [MATH: 13 \times 4] is greater than [MATH: 47.] This means that [MATH: {47}\div {13}] has a whole number part (or quotient) of [MATH: {\color{blue}3}.]

Content:
To find the remainder, we subtract the product from the dividend:

Content:
[MATH: {47} - {39} = {\color{red}8}]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: {47}\div {13} = {\color{blue}3}\,\textrm{R}\,{\color{red}8}.]

Since [MATH: \color{blue}7] plates will carry [MATH: 77] cupcakes in total, the number of cupcakes that will remain is

[MATH: 81 - 77 ={\color{red}4}.]

So we conclude that [MATH: 7] plates can be filled completely, and [MATH: 4] cupcakes will remain.
